stem.text: The graph shows the variation with force of the extension of a wire.

stem.alt: Graph of extension (vertical axis) against force (horizontal axis), origin 0. Points R (at the origin), P and Q are marked. Two curves start at R and meet at Q: a lower curve through P with arrows showing increasing force, and an upper curve with an arrow showing force decreasing. Labelled increasing force and force decreasing.

stem.text: The force is gradually increased to a maximum at Q and then gradually decreased to zero at R.

A.text: Along the line PQ, the wire obeys Hooke’s law.

B.text: Along the line RP, the spring constant is equal to $\dfrac{\text{extension}}{\text{force}}$.

C.text: The wire has elastic deformation at point Q.

D.text: The work done in stretching the wire to P is equal to (force $\times$ extension) at point P.
